name: GA-02
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Sanford Bishop has a massive fundraising edge ($1.1M raised vs $206K, $448K cash on hand)
District's Democratic lean (D+4 PVI) plus a favorable national environment
Polymarket prices Bishop at 93% to win
No public polling, but challenger Matt Day has almost no cash ($1.8K on hand)
model.rationale: Bishop combines long incumbency, a dominant money advantage, and a challenger with negligible resources in a D-leaning district, while markets price him near certain. With no polling to contradict the fundamentals, the race stays Safe Democratic.
model.watch: Any late outside spending or polling showing Bishop under 55% would warrant moving this toward Likely D.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Southwest Georgia's 2nd District has reelected Democrat Sanford Bishop for decades, and he enters the general election with a large financial advantage over Republican Matt Day. Bishop has raised over $1.1 million and holds nearly $448,000 on hand, while Day has raised about $206,000 and reports under $2,000 in cash, leaving him little ability to communicate.

The district leans Democratic by about four points, the national environment favors Democrats, and prediction markets give Bishop roughly a 93% chance of winning. No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the forecast rests on fundamentals, money, and market pricing, all of which point to a comfortable Bishop win.
